negative_findings.description: Czech-language searches for hardware-OEM reference or case-study pages (Ingenico, PAX, Verifone) returned no CZ-localised customer-reference pages from the OEMs themselves. All Czech-language hits were acquirer catalogues, accessory resellers and user manuals rather than vendor references.
negative_findings.result_summary: OEM customer references for CZ appear to exist only in English on global sites, if at all; the CZ evidence trail runs through acquirer product pages and manuals instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Terminal-OEM share in CZ cannot be read off vendor marketing and must be inferred indirectly from acquirer hardware catalogues, manuals and accessory listings - a slower, fingerprint-based method.

negative_findings.description: The Czech term 'personalizace' plus 'karty' is heavily polluted by retail marketing about personalised virtual card designs (MONETA campaigns), swamping results about industrial card production and personalisation bureaux.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only one genuine supply-chain hit (Monet+ chip-card production page) surfaced; the rest were consumer card-design press releases.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Future queries on card issuance supply chain should use narrower Czech terms such as 'výroba čipových karet', 'personalizační centrum', 'embosing' and avoid bare 'personalizace karet'.

negative_findings.description: No press release was found linking Nexi/Nets to Ceska sporitelna acquiring or processing. Nexi Central Europe states Czech Republic coverage generally, but no named CZ bank customer was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Nexi CZ presence is asserted at group level only; specific CZ bank mandates remain unidentified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The CZ processing landscape cannot yet be fully attributed between Global Payments Europe, Nexi Central Europe and in-house/bank-owned units such as BANIT; leaving this open risks mis-sizing the addressable processing market.

negative_findings.description: No press release or public statement with installed-terminal counts was found for Dotypay/Dotykacka SoftPOS in CZ despite targeted Czech-language searching.
negative_findings.result_summary: Domestic POS vendors publicise product features and subsidy participation but not fleet size.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: SoftPOS/Android-terminal penetration in CZ will have to be approximated from the MPO 'Cesko plati kartou' scheme statistics and acquirer disclosures rather than vendor claims.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching on ATM outsourcing and self-service network management for CZ banks returned consumer-facing locator and explainer content, not supplier contracts. The only quantified outsourcing evidence found came from the vendor side (Diebold Nixdorf's CSOB case study).
negative_findings.result_summary: Demand-side disclosure of ATM outsourcing is effectively absent in Czech; supply-side vendor material is the only route.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's core rationale: vendor publications, not bank publications, are the viable channel for CZ self-service procurement intelligence, and single-sourced vendor claims will need triangulation.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-in-transit and cash-cycle service providers serving CZ ATM fleets (e.g. Loomis, G4S/Brink's-type operators) were not searched in this pass, although they are a distinct vendor tier revealing cash-usage volumes and ATM servicing economics.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run Czech queries such as 'přeprava hotovosti', 'zpracování hotovosti', 'plnění bankomatů', 'CIT služby banky' plus English CIT vendor + Czech Republic queries.

coverage_gaps.description: Company-register and financial-filing sources (ARES, justice.cz Sbirka listin) were identified as a triangulation route but not actually collected. Vendor CZ subsidiaries file accounts that quantify revenue and headcount - a hard check on marketing claims.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ARES / justice.cz Sbirka listin lookups for Global Payments Europe s.r.o., Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o., Euronet Services CR, BANIT s.r.o., Monet+ a.s. and Nexi entities.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor job postings, partner/certification directories and conference/exhibitor lists (e.g. CZ banking IT conferences, ATMIA/Money20/20 exhibitor rosters) were not exploited. These indirectly reveal platform stacks and account teams per CZ bank.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically mine LinkedIn/vendor career pages for CZ-located roles naming platforms, and harvest exhibitor and speaker lists from CZ banking technology events.

coverage_gaps.description: Global vendor sites (Temenos, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, KAL, Nexi) publish CZ-relevant material almost exclusively in English; no Czech-language mirrors of these case studies were located, so Czech-only monitoring would miss the highest-value fleet statistics.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dual-track monitor: English for global vendor newsrooms and IR feeds, Czech for domestic vendors, PR wires (Protext), acquirer catalogues and procurement portals.

coverage_gaps.description: Several fleet and estate figures encountered (CSOB ~1,025 self-service devices, Ceska sporitelna 1,600+ ATMs, Euronet ~600-700 ATMs, Air Bank ~160 terminals in 2017) come from single vendor or media sources with differing vintages and no consistent definition of what counts as a device.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a fleet-metric register capturing source, date and definition for every number, and reconcile against CNB payment-infrastructure statistics before any figure is used in analysis.

brief: The CZ technology-supplier layer is unusually legible because the demand side is silent: Czech banks publish almost nothing about ATM/POS procurement, while their vendors publish named case studies with hard fleet numbers - Diebold Nixdorf on CSOB (1,025 devices under managed services), KAL on Ceska sporitelna (1,600+ ATMs, cash recyclers, QR cardless), Temenos on Komercni banka's core migration with Syncordis. The processing tier splits between Prague-based Global Payments Europe, Nexi Central Europe's CEE hub, Worldline via KB SmartPay/GoPay, and bank-owned BANIT inside CSOB, with Euronet as the dominant independent ATM deployer. Czech-language material adds what English does not: PR-wire contract announcements on Protext, acquirer terminal catalogues and manuals that fingerprint the Ingenico/Verifone/PAX installed base, and CNB's E-ZAK procurement portal for priced, named supplier records. The main weaknesses are single-sourced vendor fleet claims of inconsistent vintage, an unmapped cash-in-transit tier, and the absence of any public installed-base figures for domestic SoftPOS vendors.
